column1: # Cassandra token forms for generated compat rows: the text written for each
# token of Cql.g4 that is a class of texts. Keywords (K_*) and punctuation
# spell themselves and need no row. Each note cites the rule in Lexer.g, as
# A sample of one name, string or number stands for its class when the
# grammar judge reads a statement; a name sampled in quotes stands for names

column3: Lexer.g:374 a letter, then letters, digits and _
Lexer.g:281 a double-quoted name; "" is a quote in it
Lexer.g:256 a single-quoted string, or a $$-quoted one
Lexer.g:353 digits with a fraction or an exponent; the rule's second alternative, an integer, emits INTEGER
Lexer.g:382 a UUID in its 8-4-4-4-12 form
Lexer.g:366 a duration: digits and a unit
Parser.g:1449 a column name is written as a name: the rule lists EMPTY_QUOTED_NAME first, and every row naming a column would carry ""
Lexer.g:94 COLUMNFAMILY | TABLE: rows write TABLE, the current name, and the judge takes either
Lexer.g:96 COLUMNFAMILIES | TABLES: rows write TABLES, and the judge takes either
